newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO PESO ENDS FIRM, ZIGZAGS ON U.S. LONG BOND.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO PESO ENDS FIRM, ZIGZAGS ON U.S. LONG BOND.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer across the board on Monday after zigzagging within a narrow range amid a market tracking the U.S. long bond, dealers said.
"There was some speculation here in line with the U.S. bond market, but nothing spectacular," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.3 and 1.6 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8010/7.8070 and 7.7980/7.8010 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds stood unchanged and were yielding 6.64 percent when peso trading closed in Mexico.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.3 centavos firmer at 7.8010/7.8040 per dollar.
Dealers said they did not detect any exercising of dollar put auctions previously auction by the central bank, despite the strength of the peso making this a potentially profitable move.
Traders expected the market to follow developments in the U.S. bond market closely until publication of U.S. inflation data.
